newsitem.title: UK: More Far Eastern granting seen in LME options.
newsitem.headline: More Far Eastern granting seen in LME options.

text.p: The LME options market saw more Far Eastern granting in copper and aluminium which pressured volatility and players continued seeking nickel upside calls.

"The large volumes we saw last week haven't been repeated this week, but the Koreans have been moving again," one option trader said, referring to relentless granting since last December thought to originate in Korea.

In aluminium, fourth quarter implied volatility eased on the week by about one percentage point to be quoted around 15.5/17.00 percent, with one trader saying it traded at 16 percent on Friday after dipping to 15.5 percent earlier.
Granting of fourth quarter 1997 strangles was seen at $1,650/$1,550 strikes, one trader said.
Another dealer said there was granting of nearby $1,575/$1,600 strangles on Thursday, which traded at 19 percent volatility for March and 18 percent for April.
There was also some two-way business in nearbys and short-covering pushed volatility up to 20 percent earlier in the week, another dealer added.
In copper, volatility had eased slightly on the week by one-half to one percentage point.
"The nearby months have been sold down again and April traded down to 19.25 percent this morning," one trader said.
March and April were bid at 18.75 to 19.00 percent.
One trader said a large tranche of third and fourth quarter upside calls have been granted on copper, with offers seen at 19.75 percent.
Nickel has seen keen interest in upside calls again this week, especially on March and April, but it dried up over the past day or two, traders said.
One dealer said there had also been some interest in April puts on Thursday and another said $7,700s had traded this morning at 29.5 percent.
"We're stuck in a range and people are waiting for a break one way or the other, so people don't want to be too short of volatility if it does," one said.
Overall, volatility has remained steady on the week.
One dealer said the upsides traded up to 33.0 percent volatility but there has been a skew between calls and puts, with front month calls quoted at 30.0/33.0 percent and puts at 27.0/30.0 percent.
"More than anything that reflects the way most people's books are structured. Most of the guys are happy to buy the upsides and let this downside stuff go," a trader said.

In zinc, some consumer min/max deals had been done, with one trader seeing $1,325 calls being bought and $1,150 puts being sold, while another trader said he had done a similar deal at $1,375/$1,125 strikes.
There had also been lots of enquires for upside calls, but actual trading volumes were scant. "Dealers are very reluctant to sell upside calls," one said.
There had also been a little bit of buying of downside puts.
"This probably reflects the fact that if producers are not doing anything now, they're expected to do something soon so maybe people are covering some holes," a trader said.
Dealers had differing views of nearby volatility, with some saying March was offered as high as 26.0 percent and others had it offered at 22.25 percent.
Fourth quarter was pegged around 18.0/20.0 percent.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
